first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4%, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. This directly addresses a current funnel deterioration while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing merits verification because of the competitive threat, but its reported 30-day retention harm makes it a weaker current choice despite acquisition upside.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing this cycle: although qualified revenue rose 18%, verified 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal.

final2.rationale: Continue with shortened onboarding despite the competitor's deeper price cut. Verified evidence shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, addressing both current funnel declines while supporting sustainable revenue. The only verified pricing response—a 40% targeted SMB discount—raised qualified revenue short term but cut 30-day retention by 12% and failed at first renewal. Escalating price pressure increases uncertainty, but it does not justify using a demonstrated retention-damaging tactic under a long-term qualified-revenue objective.
